correctness.rationale: The lower bound follows because m separating formulas produce at most 2^m distinct truth vectors. For the upper bound, inject the k quotient classes into m-bit strings and define each bit by a CPC formula whose truth set is the union of classes carrying bit one. Classical finite Boolean definability makes every such union definable. The partition census is then exactly the Stirling/Bell census. A finite checker independently verifies every partition for n up to three.

value.rationale: The source frames separation as making implicit quotients explicit. The least number of Boolean coordinates is therefore a natural invariant. The theorem gives that invariant exactly, shows a sharp n-variable bound, and classifies all semantic coequivalences by rank. This is a meaningful quantitative strengthening of the source's one-formula-per-class construction rather than a renaming or isolated finite computation.
